answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by delaying privileges until an identity completes tasks checked by randomly selected, unrelated reviewers. Reviewers should verify the underlying evidence, not merely repeat each other's approval, and shared control signals should reduce trust across linked accounts. Like shale layers preserving a geological record, signed work histories expose sudden identity resets; even a whisper of coordinated behavior can trigger an audit before a new account gains influence on its voyage through the network.
